title: Sensorimotor alpha and beta ECoG during movement imagery (Stolk et al. 2019, shared participants S4-S6)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from three epilepsy patients (S4-S6) implanted with subdural grids and strips, collected while they imagined grasping a cylinder with the left or right hand. The data are a subset of the participants in Stolk et al. (2019) who gave permission to share their data, and are released as trial segments. The dataset supports investigation of alpha and beta rhythmic activity in the human sensorimotor cortex during motor imagery.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded with a 128-channel Micromed system (512 Hz, analog band-pass 0.15-134.4 Hz) using Ad-Tech subdural grids and strips with 10 mm spacing. Participants performed up to three sessions of 60 movement imagery trials. Electrodes were localised by fusing post-implantation CT with pre-operative T1 MRI and projecting onto FreeSurfer surfaces. The shared data are unfiltered trial segments stored back-to-back in BrainVision or NWB files.
